correctness.rationale: A second exponential-tilt derivative of bivariate normal crossing probability equals [ρ(a²+b²)−2ab]/(π√(1−ρ²)) for any centered jointly Gaussian linear statistic. Substitution with b_i=Σ_jρ^{|i−j|} yields an exact finite sum for all n≥2, σ²>0, |ρ|<1; geometric sums give the displayed closed expression. Exact rational symbolic evaluation, endpoint Taylor coefficients, and large-n sign examples replay in the standalone checker (413 checks). Analytic finite binomial series for ρ^n gives limits at ρ=−1+c/n² with parity, while the power ρ^n is exponentially small at ρ=−1+c/√n. For fixed positive c, these proofs justify the claimed limits and continuity gives at least two distinct even-n zeros. The signs exactly at c=12 or 1/√2 and uniqueness of roots are not asserted.

value.rationale: Zero-crossing frequency measures discrete oscillations, whereas squared sample sum measures global low-frequency mass. Their covariance quantifies statistical dependence of two natural, distinct time-series summaries and cannot be read from their marginal laws. The two negative-unit-root boundary layers at scales n^−2 and n^−1/2, with opposite even/odd microscopic signs, force a nonmonotone negative–positive–negative even-sample dependence pattern. This is a structural phase phenomenon, not just a routine fixed-number calculation, and the claim is limited to a proved existence classification without speculative applications.
